summary.text: A 14-year-old male presented to the ophthalmology outpatient department with marked visual impairment, particularly under bright light conditions. Slit-lamp examination showed a clear anterior chamber and a cataractous lens nucleus with characteristic powdery opacities, and cataracta pulverulenta was diagnosed; ectopia lentis (lens subluxation) was absent.

Systemic examination found a high-arched palate with nasal voice, increased arm span with an arm span-to-height ratio of 1.35, arachnodactyly and pectus excavatum. Echocardiography showed trace tricuspid and mitral regurgitation and a small 9 mm atrial septal defect. The revised Ghent systemic score exceeded 7, confirming Marfan syndrome.

He underwent manual small incision cataract surgery under peribulbar anesthesia after pupil dilation, with a scleral tunnel, capsulorhexis, nucleus extraction, cortical aspiration, posterior chamber intraocular lens implantation, and subconjunctival gentamicin and dexamethasone. Postoperative best-corrected visual acuity was 6/6, described as an excellent visual recovery, and the figure captions describe a clear cornea, a stable well-centered lens and a quiet anterior chamber.
